purpose: Compare the original authors' eleven CQA endpoints and decision conditions with the latest fixed system output, distinguishing endpoint overlap from executable criterion equivalence.

baseline.identity: The original manuscript authors' human-selected eleven CQAs; their values are predictions, not eleven measured clinical outcomes.
baseline.source_title: Multi-target TME Reprogramming Awakens TLS driven Immunity in Ovarian Cancer
baseline.source_locator: PDF page 4, Figure 1A(d); caption and adjacent text on pages 4-5 establish that every condition was required.
baseline.figure_identity_check: The embedded page-4 figure image has identical bytes in both supplied PDFs.
baseline.extraction_method: Direct visual inspection of PDF page 4; minimal factual endpoint, comparator and cutoff transcription. No full manuscript, figure image, original intake payload or private mapping is redistributed.
baseline.historical_intake_availability: Standalone original intake payloads and old case streams are absent from the retained store; two case-inheritance snapshots retain intake headers/digests and two historical comparison artifacts retain their old decisions. The current factual baseline was checked directly against the supplied manuscript rather than reconstructed from the old system registry.

comparison_method.scope: All 53 current working items, with the 18 enabled core rules reported separately. Historical retired/merged proposals are not counted as current matches.
comparison_method.same_named_endpoint: The original and latest definitions explicitly name the same endpoint; predictor identity may remain unknown. This alone does not make their thresholds, authority or use equivalent.
comparison_method.related_endpoint_unresolved: A related property or similar endpoint is present, but the frozen records do not establish the original event identity.
comparison_method.no_matching_endpoint: No current criterion explicitly expresses the named original endpoint.
comparison_method.full_criterion_equivalent: Requires matching operational quantity, threshold/comparator, applicability and decision semantics. No such equivalence is established in this comparison.
comparison_method.counting: The two bioavailability class rows remain distinct. One unspecified Bioavailability_Ma output is not treated as recovering both classes. Related quantities are not included in the same-named-endpoint count.

summary.interpretation: Two original endpoints are named in the current registry; one participates in the 18-rule core. The eleven-condition original screening gate is not reproduced. These are descriptive counts, not a new primary recovery score.

latest_candidates.name: Predicted oral bioavailability probability (Bioavailability_Ma)
latest_candidates.definition: Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted oral exposure.
latest_candidates.evaluation_reason: withheld from scoring while review is unresolved: q_01M52M1WS2131R5C0YG0QMTWP1: criterion remains pending under qualification_first_v1: the critic's finding stands, so the criterion does not score as proposed

latest_candidates.name: Oral bioavailability (human, measured F%)
latest_candidates.definition: Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

rows.threshold_comparison: Original probability > 0.5; Bioavailability_Ma and measured F% have no cutoff. A percent-of-dose boundary is not a probability cutoff.
rows.rationale: The manuscript names a distinct 20% bioavailability class. The current Bioavailability_Ma definition supplies no percentage class boundary. Measured F% is a different quantity from a class probability. Neither establishes this original endpoint; the generic probability is not counted twice for the two original classes.

latest_candidates.name: Predicted human intestinal absorption probability (HIA_Hou)
latest_candidates.definition: Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted intestinal absorption.

The manuscript does not identify the predictor, so numerical/model equivalence is unverified.

latest_candidates.name: Predicted skin reaction probability (exploratory)
latest_candidates.definition: ADMET-AI Skin_Reaction model output: predicted probability in [0,1] that a compound elicits a skin reaction (rash, hand-foot skin reaction). The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents that dermatologic toxicity is a frequent, dose-limiting class liability of chronically dosed oral kinase inhibitors, but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

rows.threshold_comparison: Original < 0.5; latest has no cutoff and is context only.
rows.rationale: The current Skin_Reaction item is an exploratory observation defined as rash/hand-foot skin reaction. The manuscript names skin sensitisation. Their event identity is not established by the frozen criterion; it has no cutoff and contributes no ranking weight.

latest_enabled_core.definition: Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.

latest_enabled_core.name: Predicted logP (RDKit)
latest_enabled_core.definition: Model-predicted logP (RDKit); lower values are preferred because lipophilic, poorly soluble agents show food-dependent and variable oral absorption.

latest_enabled_core.definition: Number of PAINS alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of assay interference and poor drug-likeness.

latest_enabled_core.name: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax, median of reported values)
latest_enabled_core.definition: Median of reported times to maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours; when a source reports only a range, the range midpoint is used. Lower values indicate faster absorption. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.

latest_enabled_context.definition: Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

latest_enabled_context.name: Predicted aqueous solubility (log mol/L)
latest_enabled_context.definition: Model-predicted aqueous solubility in log(mol/L) from the ADMET-AI Solubility_AqSolDB model; recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report solubility as a generic drug-like property and give low-solubility examples, without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

latest_enabled_context.definition: Model-predicted apparent permeability coefficient across Caco-2 monolayers from the ADMET-AI Caco2_Wang endpoint, in log(10^-6 cm/s); recorded as a descriptive consideration because the cited claims report low permeability for specific poorly absorbed compounds without validating this endpoint or establishing a direction for this library.

latest_enabled_context.name: Predicted clinical toxicity probability (exploratory)
latest_enabled_context.definition: ADMET-AI ClinTox model output: predicted probability in [0,1] of clinical toxicity. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents general toxicity and dose-limiting adverse events for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

limits: This post-hoc documentation is separate from the pre-registered, isolated recovery route; B is not remeasured.
The two retained historical readings use different frozen sets, intake digests and equivalence judgments; they are preserved as separate results rather than a performance trend.
The manuscript panel lacks model and event details needed to establish numerical equivalence; no missing detail is inferred from current predictor names.

The original 3171-compound/140-predicted-binder cascade and the latest 3177-candidate evidence-based evaluation have different populations and screening policies. Surufatinib's latest rank does not measure CQA overlap.
No criterion, threshold, source record, historical decision or visibility flag was changed for this comparison.
